title: Linux Foundation launches Tokenomics Foundation to standardize AI infrastructure economics
summary: On June 3, 2026, the Linux Foundation announced the Tokenomics Foundation, a new standards body backed by Accenture, Booking.com, Google Cloud, IBM, JPMorganChase, Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, and ServiceNow. The foundation will develop open specifications for measuring token efficiency, benchmarking AI costs, and governing token-based spending across the supply chain. Operating in close partnership with the FinOps Foundation, it extends cloud financial management disciplines into token-based AI economics. Goldman Sachs projects global token usage will multiply 24x by 2030 to 120 quadrillion tokens per month, and inference market revenues are expected to grow from $106 billion (2025) to $255 billion by 2030. The foundation's inaugural conference, Tokenomicon, is scheduled for San Diego in June 2027.
whyItMatters: The founding member list (Google, Microsoft, IBM, JPMorgan, SAP, Salesforce) signals that token cost governance has reached board-level urgency — this is no longer a niche FinOps concern but a mainstream enterprise priority.

Without common metrics, organizations cannot reliably compare AI tool costs, benchmark efficiency across models, or audit vendor billing claims. Open standards will enable informed procurement and vendor negotiation for the first time.

AI token spend is the fastest-growing line item on enterprise technology budgets, yet most organizations lack the instrumentation to connect token consumption to business outcomes — the foundation aims to close this gap.
recommendedActions: Begin tracking token consumption per team, per model, and per use case now, using whatever tooling is available, so you can adopt foundation standards from a data-informed baseline.
Align your AI FinOps function with the FOCUS specification (the foundation's planned extension) to prepare for standardized token cost reporting.
risksAndCaveats: Standards bodies are slow; usable specifications may take 12–18 months. Organizations need interim governance frameworks now, not after standards emerge.
The foundation is industry-led, and founding members include both major AI providers and consumers — standards may reflect compromises that favor provider interests over consumer transparency.
The 24x usage growth projection from Goldman Sachs assumes continued adoption acceleration, which could slow if cost governance tightens or AI ROI proves harder to demonstrate than expected.
